episode.title: Add bounded, workspace-scoped working-tree diff review
episode.before: At parent a0ce04a9929527a7884422842a8079e0af99ead0, the core could compute aggregate working-tree statistics and whole-tree hunks, but it had no on-demand single-file hunk operation. The daemon had no working-tree diff REST routes or SDK methods, and the web shell had no Changes dialog, workspace-scoped diff state, or local /diff navigation.
episode.after: Commit 582fb49603c74158e13f735cdfa97e987d0c58d2 adds a read-only review path from core through daemon routes and SDK to the web shell. It lists changed files with bounded statistics, lazily fetches normalized single-file hunks, synthesizes bounded hunks for regular untracked text files, preserves rename and no-newline semantics, exposes truncation, rejects unsafe paths and untrusted workspaces, and renders expandable per-file changes with independent old/new-side highlighting, loading/error states, and workspace-correct navigation from /diff, the active status chip, or a sidebar workspace.
episode.diff: The implementation adds workspace Git-diff list and single-file routes, registers their bound and workspace-qualified variants, adds optional additive SDK wire types and client methods, extends core diff parsing and retrieval for per-file lazy loading, and introduces a Changes dialog plus entry-point state in the web shell. Supporting tests cover route serialization and trust gates, SDK URL encoding, rename-aware retrieval, traversal rejection, tracked and untracked truncation, FIFO avoidance, lazy expansion, syntax highlighting, failure degradation, hidden-file notices, and /diff interception.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned implementation commit is 582fb49603c74158e13f735cdfa97e987d0c58d2, with parent a0ce04a9929527a7884422842a8079e0af99ead0, and describes a read-only Changes dialog, daemon REST access, workspace trust gating, and optional additive SDK fields.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller --stat 582fb49603c74158e13f735cdfa97e987d0c58d2; issue-bundle.json linked_pull_requests[0].commits[0] and commit_show_stat

evidence_units.claim: The parent contains fetchGitDiffHunks for whole-tree retrieval but has neither fetchGitDiffHunksForFile nor the daemon diff route, web-shell GitDiffDialog, or App-level diff navigation state.
evidence_units.source: git show a0ce04a9929527a7884422842a8079e0af99ead0:packages/core/src/utils/gitDiff.ts lines 279-306; git cat-file -e parent:packages/cli/src/serve/routes/workspace-git-diff.ts; git cat-file -e parent:packages/web-shell/client/components/dialogs/GitDiffDialog.tsx; git show parent:packages/web-shell/client/App.tsx

evidence_units.claim: The core adds fetchGitDiffHunksForFile, which normalizes caller paths to repository-relative paths, rejects traversal or outside-root paths, avoids transient Git states, uses rename detection when oldPath is supplied, and disables external diff and text-conversion execution.

Single-file retrieval synthesizes an all-added hunk only for Git-confirmed untracked files, checks that the target is a regular file before opening it, avoids following unsafe file types, detects binary content, and applies byte and line caps while returning an explicit truncated flag.

Diff list and parser contracts retain at most 50 file details, cap individual diff content at 1,000,000 bytes and 400 lines, preserve the post-rename path as the key with oldPath metadata, preserve no-newline markers, and record files whose displayed hunks were truncated.

Core tests verify new-path rename keying, no-newline marker handling, truncation tracking, transient-state rejection, rename-aware old-to-new retrieval, untracked synthesis, tracked and untracked truncation, binary handling, FIFO non-blocking behavior, traversal rejection, and acceptance of a literal ..foo filename.

The daemon exposes list and single-file read routes, applies no-store read headers, serializes oldPath and truncation metadata, validates the required path query, and supports an optional oldPath query for rename-aware retrieval.
Workspace-qualified diff routes resolve the requested runtime and require it to be trusted before invoking either list or single-file retrieval.

Route tests verify list and hunk serialization, oldPath propagation, additive truncated output, missing-path rejection, trusted workspace selection, rejection of untrusted and unknown workspaces, and unavailable output for traversal rejected by the core.
The TypeScript SDK adds workspaceGitDiff and workspaceGitDiffFile methods for bound and workspace-qualified clients and URL-encodes both current and pre-rename paths.
SDK tests verify diff-list deserialization and single-file URL construction with and without oldPath, including the workspace-qualified route.

The web dialog first loads the bounded file list, then fetches hunks only when a non-binary row is expanded; it forwards oldPath, keys rows by workspace and current path, and presents loading, unavailable, empty, binary, error, hidden-file, and truncated states.

Rendered rows maintain old and new line numbers, preserve meta rows, tokenize old and new sides independently, fall back to plain text when highlighting fails, and surface unexpected row-building failures instead of leaving an empty view.

Dialog tests verify file statistics, hidden-count disclosure, lazy expansion, StrictMode loading recovery, rename propagation, unavailable and clean states, binary and untracked labels, list and per-file failures, truncation disclosure, malformed-hunk degradation, and per-side syntax token use.

App state stores the workspace selected for review, intercepts /diff locally instead of forwarding it to the agent, targets the same active workspace used by status polling, renders GitDiffDialog, and passes a workspace-specific open callback to the sidebar.
The App test verifies that submitting /diff opens the Changes dialog and does not forward the command to the agent.

The implementation includes direct unit and route-level oracles across the core parser/retriever, daemon routes, SDK client, dialog component, and App command integration; the evidence bundle identifies the case as implementation_plus_test and a train candidate.

candidate_atomics.name: compute_bounded_single_file_diff
candidate_atomics.title: Compute a safe, bounded diff for one changed file
candidate_atomics.description: Normalize a requested file within the repository, compute only that file's working-tree change, preserve rename and no-newline semantics, synthesize regular untracked text as additions, and disclose when caps make the result incomplete.

semantic_action.intent: Provide expandable line-level review data without computing or transferring the entire working-tree diff and without allowing path escape or blocking special-file reads.
semantic_action.module_role: working-tree diff computation and normalization layer
semantic_action.pre_state: A caller has a repository workspace and a current file path, optionally with its pre-rename path; the file may be tracked, renamed, deleted, untracked, binary, unchanged, unsafe, or temporarily unavailable during a Git operation.
semantic_action.post_state: The caller receives normalized structured hunks for the requested repository file, or a null/unavailable result for invalid or unsupported cases; any content cut by byte or line limits is explicitly marked truncated.
semantic_action.validation: Core tests assert rename-aware edits, traversal rejection, transient-state rejection, untracked synthesis, binary and FIFO handling, no-newline preservation, and tracked/untracked truncation reporting.

candidate_atomics.name: expose_trusted_diff_read_contract
candidate_atomics.title: Expose diff review through a trusted read-only workspace contract
candidate_atomics.description: Publish bounded list and per-file diff operations through workspace-aware endpoints and client methods while preserving metadata, URL encoding, cache controls, and trust boundaries.

semantic_action.intent: Let a review client request changed-file summaries and lazy file hunks for the intended workspace without granting access to untrusted workspaces or leaking path parameters into route syntax.
semantic_action.module_role: workspace-scoped read API and client adaptation layer
semantic_action.pre_state: Core diff operations exist, but consumers need a stable workspace-qualified transport contract for list and per-file retrieval.
semantic_action.post_state: Bound and workspace-qualified clients can retrieve serialized diff summaries and hunks; current and old paths round-trip safely, untrusted or unknown workspaces are rejected, and capped content remains identifiable.
semantic_action.validation: Route tests exercise serialization, query validation, trust gating, workspace selection, traversal degradation, and truncation; SDK tests verify encoded URLs and response deserialization.

candidate_atomics.name: render_lazy_review_surface
candidate_atomics.title: Render an expandable diff review surface with explicit degradation states
candidate_atomics.description: Load a bounded changed-file list, fetch file hunks only on expansion, render line numbers and per-side highlighting, and show incomplete, unavailable, loading, empty, binary, and failure states explicitly.

semantic_action.intent: Make working-tree changes reviewable without eagerly loading every file and without silently showing empty or incomplete content when retrieval, tokenization, or limits intervene.
semantic_action.pre_state: A workspace-scoped diff client can return a changed-file summary and on-demand structured hunks.
semantic_action.post_state: Reviewers can expand individual files and distinguish additions, deletions, context, meta markers, renames, hidden files, truncation, binary files, loading, clean/unavailable repositories, and recoverable failures.
semantic_action.validation: Component tests cover lazy retrieval, rename forwarding, StrictMode remounts, file-list and per-file errors, malformed hunks, truncation notices, hidden counts, binary/untracked labels, and successful per-side tokenization.

candidate_atomics.name: route_review_entry_to_workspace
candidate_atomics.title: Route every review entry point to the intended workspace
candidate_atomics.description: Resolve the active or explicitly selected workspace before opening review, keep that workspace in dialog state, and consume the local review command without sending it to the agent.

semantic_action.intent: Ensure review navigation opens the changes belonging to the workspace the user selected, including multi-workspace and pre-session contexts.
semantic_action.module_role: review navigation and workspace ownership layer
semantic_action.pre_state: The application may have an active session workspace, a selected next-session workspace, or a workspace-specific sidebar entry, and a user activates a diff command or status affordance.
semantic_action.post_state: The review dialog is opened with one explicit workspace identifier; /diff is handled locally, sidebar entries retain their own workspace, and absence of a workspace is surfaced instead of forwarding an unintended prompt.
semantic_action.validation: The App test proves /diff opens the Changes dialog without agent forwarding; App call sites share active workspace resolution and pass workspace-specific open callbacks.

candidate_workflows.name: add_bounded_workspace_diff_review
candidate_workflows.title: Add bounded, workspace-correct change review
candidate_workflows.description: An executable resolution chain for adding a read-only change-review surface that is safe on large or hostile working trees, lazy at file granularity, and correctly scoped across multiple workspaces.

workflow_graph.goal: Allow a user to navigate from a workspace-aware entry point to a read-only changed-file list and expand individual files into bounded, accurate line-level diffs with explicit incomplete and failure states.
when_to_use: A client must review local working-tree changes through a remote, daemon, browser, or otherwise separated presentation layer.
Whole-tree diff retrieval is too expensive or unsafe, so detailed content should be loaded only for the file being reviewed.
The application can address more than one workspace and review actions must retain workspace ownership.
anti_goals: Do not mutate the working tree, index, branch, stash, or repository configuration.
Do not eagerly fetch or syntax-highlight every file in the working tree.
Do not silently present capped content as a complete diff.
Do not bypass workspace trust checks or permit path traversal.
Do not forward a local review-navigation command to an agent or command executor.
not_applicable_when: The product only needs aggregate change counts and no line-level review.
The source cannot provide structured or parseable working-tree changes.
There is no trustworthy workspace or repository boundary against which requested paths can be normalized.
The requested surface is intended to edit, stage, discard, or commit changes rather than remain read-only.
inputs: current file path and optional pre-rename path
file, byte, and line presentation limits
review entry points and dialog host
workflow_graph.entry_state: The system may expose aggregate change information or whole-tree hunks, but it lacks a complete workspace-scoped path from review navigation to bounded, on-demand per-file presentation.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Each authorized review entry opens the intended workspace's changed-file list; individual rows retrieve safe bounded hunks only when expanded; rename, untracked, deleted, binary, no-newline, hidden-count, truncation, loading, clean, unavailable, and failure states are distinguishable.

steps.condition: Always required when detailed review content is not already available through a safe bounded per-file operation.
steps.validation: Exercise tracked edits, renames, untracked text, binary and special files, transient repository states, traversal attempts, no-newline markers, and both byte and line caps.

steps.condition: Required when the presentation layer does not execute in the same trust and process boundary as the repository reader.
steps.validation: Verify list and hunk serialization, path encoding, old-path propagation, no-store headers, workspace selection, missing queries, trust rejection, and additive truncation metadata.

steps.condition: Required for an interactive visual review surface.
steps.validation: Verify initial list loading, expansion-triggered file retrieval, line mapping, rename display, per-side highlighting, plain-text fallback, remount safety, hidden counts, truncation notes, and explicit error/empty/unavailable states.

steps.condition: Required when review can be opened from commands, active-workspace controls, or workspace-specific navigation.
steps.validation: Verify every entry point passes the intended workspace, local commands are consumed locally, and missing workspace state produces user feedback rather than an unintended request.

validation_ladder: Unit-test normalization and parsing invariants, including rename keys, meta markers, caps, traversal, transient states, untracked files, binary files, and non-regular files.
Route-test trust gating, required parameters, selected workspace propagation, serialization, cache headers, unavailable results, and truncation metadata.
Client-test URL encoding and response deserialization with and without a pre-rename path.
Component-test lazy loading, state transitions, per-side rendering, remount cancellation behavior, error degradation, hidden counts, and truncation disclosure.
Integration-test each navigation entry point to confirm it opens the intended workspace and does not trigger unrelated agent execution.
stop_conditions: Stop if no stable repository root or workspace trust boundary can be established.
Stop if unsafe paths can reach filesystem reads or diff execution outside the repository.
Stop if content limits exist but the client cannot distinguish truncated output from complete output.
Stop if workspace identity is lost between the navigation entry point, API call, and rendered row.
Stop if the only available validation is a title, design document, or commit message without implementation and test oracles.
unresolved_or_deferred: The evidence bundle does not include CI status checks, PR reviews, or author discussion.
No browser end-to-end performance measurement is included; bounded constants, lazy retrieval, and component tests establish the implemented control strategy but not a measured latency target.
Pattern induction and holdout promotion are deferred because this episode supplies only one repository workflow.

unresolved_questions: The GitHub issue/PR body, comments, reviews, timeline, and status checks are unavailable in the supplied bundle, so rationale beyond commit text and code comments cannot be attributed to review discussion.
The checkout worktree is not materialized at the pinned commit; evidence was read directly from Git objects at the pinned commit and parent.
No cross-repository Resolution Pattern is emitted because the extraction contract forbids inducing one from a single Issue or Workflow.
